title: The Iron Compass
premise: In 1893, Yara Zhou keeps the lighthouse at Greyhaven Point, a widowed immigrant who has spent a decade making herself unremarkable in a town that prefers her that way. When the army requisitions the harbor during the year of the great storms, they also seize the town ledger—the only record of who lived, worked, and died on the coast—and begin rewriting it to justify what comes next. Yara, who once transcribed shipping records for her late husband and knows exactly how documents lie, secretly rebuilds the true ledger from memory, salvaged papers, and the testimony of neighbors the army would rather erase. As storms cut the coast off from the capital and the garrison's commander grows desperate to control the narrative before relief ships arrive, Yara must smuggle the real record aboard the first vessel through the breakwater. The book ends with the truth published in the capital's papers while Yara, having finally claimed her own name in print, lights the lamp again—no longer invisible, but no longer alone.
about_author: R. M. Blackwood is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent fifteen years cataloguing coastal ledgers and lighthouse logs along the North Atlantic seaboard. They write historical fiction about the people history files under 'miscellaneous.'

chapters.title: The Lamp and the Ledger
chapters.summary: Yara Zhou tends the Greyhaven Point light through an ordinary autumn storm, establishing her routines, her grief for her husband Tomas, and her careful habit of being overlooked by the townspeople of Greyhaven. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: quiet loneliness mistaken for contentment; the reader sees how deliberately she has made herself small.

chapters.title: Requisition
chapters.summary: Soldiers arrive under Captain Aldous Vane with orders to fortify the harbor for the war effort; they seize warehouses, billet troops in homes, and confiscate the town ledger as 'military records.' Yara watches from the gallery of the lighthouse, unnoticed. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: dread beneath compliance—the moment invisibility stops being safety.

chapters.title: What the Ink Erases
chapters.summary: Vane's clerks begin amending the ledger: debts struck out, deaths reclassified, a drowned fisherman recast as a deserter. Yara, asked to transcribe copies because of her neat hand, recognizes forgery when she sees it. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: cold recognition—she knows exactly how documents lie, because she was trained by one.

chapters.title: The Widow's Circle
chapters.summary: Yara quietly gathers those the amendments erase: Marta the fishwife whose son is now a 'deserter,' old Pieter the pilot, and schoolteacher Edith Crane. In Edith's back room they compare memories against the official record. POV: Yara, with Edith's account embedded. Emotional beat: the fragile, frightening birth of found family among the erased.

chapters.title: Storm Season
chapters.summary: The first great storm batters the coast; the garrison demands the light stay lit for naval traffic even as fishing boats founder. Yara saves three sailors against Vane's explicit order not to signal. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: defiance crystallizes—she chooses people over orders, and cannot go back.

chapters.title: A Name in the Margin
chapters.summary: Searching Tomas's old papers, Yara finds his marginalia proving the garrison's casualty figures are falsified to hide a munitions accident that killed civilians. She begins rebuilding the true ledger page by page. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: grief transformed into purpose; Tomas's ghost becomes her collaborator.

chapters.title: The Informer
chapters.summary: Someone reports the widow's circle; Pieter is arrested and the safe house searched. Yara realizes the traitor may be someone she trusts, and Vane offers her immunity if she names the others. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: terror and temptation—the price of staying invisible dangled one last time.

chapters.title: Cut Off
chapters.summary: The worst storm of the year severs the telegraph line; Greyhaven is isolated, and Vane, expecting no witnesses, moves to burn the original ledger and silence the circle permanently. Yara hides the reconstructed record inside the lighthouse itself. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: siege mentality; the stakes become survival, not just truth.

chapters.title: The First Ship Through
chapters.summary: Climax: a relief ship fights through the breakwater. While Vane stages a triumphant inspection, Yara and Edith smuggle the true ledger aboard via the rescued sailors, and Yara confronts Vane in the lamp room as he tries to extinguish the light itself. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: fury and clarity—she signs her own name to the record in front of him.

chapters.title: On the Record
chapters.summary: Weeks later, the capital's newspapers print the true account; Vane faces inquiry, Pieter is freed, and the restored ledger returns to Greyhaven with Yara's name entered as its keeper of record. She lights the lamp for the winter fleet, surrounded by her chosen family. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: hard-won belonging—history happened to her after all, and now it carries her name.
